title: OLIX raises $312M at $3.3B for photonic AI inference chips, backed by UK Sovereign AI Fund
subtitle: The largest semiconductor VC round ever raised by a European company — Fundomo led, Arm and Reed Hastings joined, and the DX-1 chip claims 10,000 tokens per second per user on 100B-parameter models without HBM.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: London-based OLIX closed a $312 million Series B on August 3 at a $3.3 billion valuation. The round was led by New York venture firm Fundomo, with new participation from Arm, Hudson River Trading, Netflix co-founder Reed Hastings, and the UK government's Sovereign AI Fund. Existing backers Hummingbird Ventures, Crane, Plural, Creandum, Phoenix Court, and Transition all expanded their positions. It is the largest semiconductor venture round ever raised by a European company, and it comes just over two years after OLIX was founded. First customer systems are targeted for the second half of 2027.

OLIX's DX-1 is a photonic inference chip — what the company calls an Optical Tensor Processing Unit, or OTPU. Instead of using electricity to do the matrix multiplications that power large language models, the DX-1 does the math with light. It is designed to store an entire model in fast on-chip SRAM, which lets OLIX skip both advanced 2.5D packaging and high-bandwidth memory entirely. The company claims over 10,000 tokens per second per user for 100-billion-parameter models. If that number survives contact with third-party benchmarks, it is roughly an order of magnitude above what today's GPU-based inference stacks deliver at comparable model sizes.

The broader significance is the HBM bottleneck. High-bandwidth memory is the choke point of the current AI stack — supply-constrained, dominated by SK Hynix and Samsung, and the reason Nvidia's roadmap has to line up around memory yields. Any chip that credibly skips HBM changes the physics of the datacenter — less power, less packaging complexity, different supply chain, different geography. The UK government's decision to write a check through its Sovereign AI Fund puts national industrial policy behind the bet, and Arm's participation reads as its own vote of confidence in an architecture that competes directly with the Nvidia stack Arm is currently a supplier to.

For learners: when you hear photonic AI chip, ask two questions before you get excited. Does it still need HBM to run the model, and how large is the on-chip SRAM budget. Those two numbers set the ceiling on real-world token throughput more reliably than any headline TOPS or watts-per-flop figure. Also ask when the first customer systems ship. The gap between a Series B announcement and a working chip in a customer datacenter is typically two to four years — and most photonic startups have missed it.
